observations.claim: The left hand holds the black motor housing steady against the workbench surface.
The left thumb maintains contact with the side of the black housing throughout the interval.
A silver wrench and orange screwdriver lie on the table but are not touched by the left hand.
The right hand supports the lower part of the assembly while the left hand stabilizes the upper section.

uncertainties: Whether the left hand applies rotational force or only static pressure cannot be determined from the static frames.
Visibility of the exact contact point between the left thumb and the housing is partially obscured by shadows.

request_metadata.prompt:
You are documenting visible industrial assembly actions for a research dataset. You receive timestamped frames, a target hand and a target interval, but no action or error label. Observe only what is visible INSIDE the target interval. Outside frames provide context only and must be explicitly described as before/after. Describe the target hand's interaction rather than listing the whole workbench. Do not infer anomaly labels, intentions, engineering specifications, hidden causes, force, torque, or active duration from sparse images. Do not name nut sizes such as M4/M6 or internal component types unless a readable marking or unambiguous visual feature supports them; say small nut/metal part instead. Distinguish tools lying nearby from tools actually used, and tools from components. State what cannot be seen.
Return only valid JSON with this structure:
{"observations":[{"id":"O1","claim":"concise visible fact","evidence_ids":["focus_full_000"],"visibility":"clear|partial"}],"uncertainties":["..."],"needs_refinement":false,"refinement_reason":""}
Request refinement only when additional frames inside the target interval could resolve tool identity, contact, movement, or placement. Do not request refinement to recover missing engineering requirements or operator intentions. Use at most 5 concise observations, each at most 25 words; cite at most 3 provided frame IDs per observation. Report the key motion and its visible outcome without guessing.

Every frame is explicitly labeled TARGET, CONTEXT_BEFORE or CONTEXT_AFTER. Base target observations on TARGET frames. Do not move an action seen only in context into the target interval. State before/after explicitly for contextual observations. If the target hand is occluded, say so; do not substitute the other hand.

All initial frames in this version are inside the target interval. The last four images enlarge the lower workspace at timestamps already present; they are NOT later actions. Compare the target fingertips and contact points across early, middle and late frames. A nearly fixed palm can still pinch, turn, press or adjust a tiny part. Do not replace these motions with generic holding. Prioritize a change of contact or object state at the beginning, even if later frames show holding. Describe uncertain small objects generically. Lack of visible motion in a few frames is not evidence that the hand was static throughout. If the hand is partly outside the image, report incomplete visibility. Never invent absence of motion.

payload.frame_scope: Context frames can show other actions; evaluate only the stated target hand/action interval.
